data.name: Cairn UI

images.caption: Data table, calendar and toasts, dark theme

content: A modern, accessible {{Flutter component library}} built on a design token system that is actually engineered.
Colours are authored in {{OKLCH}} with a matched dark theme, the radius scale is derived proportionally from a single number, and the type scale survives text scaling.
{{65 components}}, no runtime dependencies beyond Flutter itself, and {{golden tests}} in both themes holding all of it in place.
highlights: No component hardcodes a number that should come from a token
Every place CSS-shaped design meets Flutter's rendering model is resolved explicitly and documented
80 golden images lock the light and dark output down

data.name: Flutter MCP Toolkit
data.tagline: 12 MCP servers for the Flutter lifecycle

images.caption: Real CLI output: indexing a Flutter project
Real CLI output: a mobile security scan
Real CLI output: Flutter Engineering MCP gateway

content: Twelve {{Model Context Protocol}} servers covering the {{Flutter/mobile development lifecycle}}, plus one generic CLI client that speaks to all of them over the real protocol.

Codebase intelligence, UI testing on real devices, crash analysis, {{Crashlytics}}, architecture review, dependency management, {{mobile security}}, API contract checking, test coverage, performance, {{CI/CD}} and code migration.

A {{Flutter Engineering MCP gateway}} connects to all twelve as an MCP client and re-exposes their tools behind {{one connection}}, so an agent like Claude Code can drive a Flutter project's entire toolchain.
highlights: Indexes widgets, BLoC/Cubit/Riverpod state, routes and the import graph
Flags Clean Architecture layering violations and compares OpenAPI specs against Dart models
Each server is an independently installable Python package over stdio

data.name: Cairn Site
data.tagline: Docs site for Cairn UI, built with Cairn UI
content: The marketing and documentation site for Cairn UI, a {{Flutter web app}} whose own chrome is built {{with the library it documents}}.

Nav, tabs, the {{Ctrl+K command palette}}, dialogs, toasts and the directory data table are all Cairn widgets doing a real job. If a component regresses upstream, this site breaks, and that is the point.
It ships every component as a live preview, five composed blocks, and {{five whole-app templates}}: e-commerce, dashboard, blog, docs and SaaS landing.
highlights: Dogfooding surfaced and fixed a latent crash in CairnContextMenu upstream
Deep-linkable routes on GitHub Pages via a 404.html SPA fallback
CI plus automated deploy workflows

data.name: MCP Toolkit AI
data.tagline: 17 MCP servers, a gateway, and a CLI

images.caption: Real CLI output: the gateway connected to 17 backends
Real CLI output: listing tools and calling one

content: Seventeen {{Model Context Protocol}} servers: five general-purpose ones (semantic code search, safe SQL, GitHub Issues, dev-environment awareness, a Markdown knowledge base) plus the {{twelve Flutter/mobile servers}} from Flutter MCP Toolkit.
A {{gateway}} connects to every server as an MCP client and re-exposes all their tools behind {{one endpoint}}, namespaced so names never collide.
One generic CLI speaks to all of them over the real protocol, and Agent Ops Dashboard's agents use them as tools.
highlights: A backend that fails to start is skipped with a warning instead of taking the gateway down
Read-only SQL is sqlparse-validated, row-capped and timeout-enforced
Semantic code search with local sentence-transformers embeddings and Chroma

data.name: Agent Ops Dashboard

images.caption: Live run timeline: tool calls and real results
A run mid-flight, with a Stop button

content: Submit a task in plain English and watch a {{Claude-powered agent}} work it live. Every tool call, result and reasoning step streams to the dashboard as it happens, with {{multiple runs in flight}} at once.

A {{dual agent engine}} picks the official Claude Agent SDK when an API key is set, or a headless Claude Code CLI subprocess otherwise. Both normalise into one event stream, so persistence, the {{WebSocket relay}} and the UI never know which engine ran.
The agents call {{MCP Toolkit AI}}'s servers as tools, tying the series together.
highlights: Engine choice is automatic: Agent SDK with an API key, headless Claude Code CLI without one
Runs execute as background tasks, so POST /runs returns 202 immediately
Packaged as an Electron desktop app

data.name: DocuChat AI
data.tagline: Chat with your documents, with citations
content: A full-stack {{retrieval-augmented generation}} app. It ingests PDFs, text and Markdown, chunks and embeds them {{locally}}, retrieves the most relevant passages, and {{streams a cited answer}} back from Claude.
Embeddings run on-device with sentence-transformers and the vector store is embedded {{Chroma}}, so the whole thing runs with zero external services besides the Claude API.
{{JWT}} auth with documents scoped per user, and typed end to end with mypy and strict TypeScript.
highlights: Streaming answers over SSE with inline citations back to the source chunk
pytest + httpx on the backend, Vitest + Testing Library on the frontend
One-command Docker Compose setup

data.name: PRReview AI
data.tagline: AI code review for GitHub pull requests

images.caption: A review with severity-ranked findings (demo data)
Pull request feed for a connected repo (demo data)

content: Connect a repo, open a PR, and prreview-ai fetches the diff, {{reviews it with Claude}}, and shows the findings in a dashboard.
A signed {{GitHub webhook}} triggers each review as a background task. Findings come back as {{schema-validated JSON}} with file, line and severity, not scraped from free-text model output.
{{Read-only by default}}: publishing the review as a real PR comment is a separate, explicit Post to GitHub action.
highlights: Reuses the local Claude Code login via headless claude -p, so no per-token billing to try it
HMAC-verified webhooks and Fernet-encrypted stored tokens
The AI engine and GitHub API are both faked in tests

data.name: LocalChat AI
data.tagline: A ChatGPT-like desktop app on a local model
content: A desktop chat app that runs entirely against a {{self-hosted local model}}: no API key, no per-token cost, {{no data leaving the machine}}.
{{Ollama}} serves a quantized Qwen2.5-Coder 7B on consumer hardware (an RTX 3060). The app around it adds persistence, token streaming, a real {{Stop button}}, and an {{Electron}} shell.
highlights: Fixed a bug where a client abort cancelled the stream and silently dropped the partial reply, by persisting in a finally block
Model is swappable per conversation
Shows Ollama's own tokens/sec stat after each reply

data.name: GenUI Flutter
data.tagline: Prompts compiled into native Flutter widgets

images.caption: The renderer drawing the README's profile-card spec
A sign-in form spec, with real typed-into fields
A settings spec: switches, slider, dropdown

content: Describe an interface in plain language. Claude returns a {{structured UI specification}}, and the app compiles it into {{real, native Flutter widgets at runtime}}.
Not a screenshot, not a WebView, not generated source that needs a rebuild. A generated text field is a real TextField, and a generated submit button reads back what you typed.
The model is forced into a {{tool call}} with a recursive JSON Schema, so the response is structured data. The codec that decodes it is the explicit {{trust boundary}}.
highlights: Offline history stored in Hive
Retries, backoff and error classification in the API client
Firebase Analytics, Crashlytics and Remote Config wired in

data.name: Roam

images.caption: Design: Home, Explore, Why 96% Match and Offline Mode
Design: Welcome, Smart Itinerary, Trip Map and Trip Overview
Design: Home: next trip, ready offline
Design: Offline mode with pending sync

content: Plan trips, discover places matched to your interests, navigate, and manage documents and expenses, {{with no connection at all}}.

The differentiator is a {{deterministic, explainable recommendation engine}} that scores places against your interests, reviews, distance, budget and itinerary, and tells you why: {{96% Match}}, strong coffee and anime match, close to your next stop.

The local SQLite database is the {{source of truth}}. Every mutation is one atomic transaction with an outbox row, sync is {{idempotent by construction}}, and conflicts are resolved per entity type, never silently.
highlights: Flutter + BLoC + Drift on device, a Go modular monolith on PostgreSQL + PostGIS behind it
Versioned, checksummed offline trip packages and real offline map regions
On-device full-text search over everything downloaded, built phase by phase over 100+ commits

data.name: Jaspr Web Template
content: A production-shaped web template built with {{Jaspr}}, the Dart framework that compiles components to {{real DOM}} and renders them on the server.
The demo app, Meridian, pairs a server-rendered marketing site with an authenticated dashboard behind {{httpOnly-cookie sessions}} resolved before render.
{{Islands architecture}}: only seven components ship JavaScript. The entire marketing site works with JavaScript disabled.
highlights: Offline support via a hand-written service worker
SEO done properly: canonical, Open Graph, JSON-LD, sitemap and real 404 status
224 tests plus a production build smoke test in CI

data.name: Go Starter Kit

images.caption: Swagger UI rendering the hand-written openapi.yaml
Real run: go vet, build and 141 passing tests

content: The repository you fork when starting a new backend service and you don't want to spend two weeks rebuilding {{auth, migrations, observability and CI}}.
{{chi}} router, {{pgx + sqlc}} type-safe queries instead of an ORM, embedded golang-migrate migrations, and plain {{constructor injection}} wired in one readable function.
JWT access tokens plus opaque refresh tokens with {{rotation and reuse detection}}, RBAC on admin routes, and RFC 9457 problem documents mapped in exactly one place.
highlights: Hand-written OpenAPI 3 spec with a generated typed Go client
Feature flags with single-flight cache refresh and stable percentage rollouts
Idempotency keys, per-request timeouts and graceful shutdown

data.name: FastAPI Starter Kit

images.caption: Swagger UI rendering the committed openapi.json
Real run: 213 tests passing, ruff clean

content: A production-oriented {{FastAPI}} template built around {{hexagonal architecture}}, so you don't relitigate the same twenty decisions on every new API.
The layering is enforced by ruff {{and by tests that walk the AST}}. PostgreSQL with async SQLAlchemy 2.0 and Alembic sits behind Protocol ports.
JWT with refresh rotation and reuse detection, DB-backed {{feature flags}}, idempotency keys, structlog, rate limiting and security headers, all behind one error envelope.
highlights: 227 tests, mypy --strict, migration round-trip and a container smoke test in CI
Committed openapi.json with a generated typed Python client, kept in sync by CI
A real dependency_overrides testing pattern from one composition root
